zh.question: 把橡皮筋绷紧，和把它拨得更大，听到的变化是同一件事吗？
zh.observe: 播放慢镜头并切换空气视图，盯住金色小团和空心圈。暂停、回看声源停止后的片段，再单独听两种张力或幅度的实际音高。

academic.title: 振动传递扰动而非运走空气
academic.body: 橡皮筋振动带动附近空气，产生向外传播的压强和密度变化。空气中的声波通常是纵波，空气小团的平均位移方向与传播方向平行；这与弯曲弦的横向位移不同。图中实心点表示小团空气的平均位置，不是单个分子的热运动轨迹。扰动携带能量向远处走，小团空气在平衡位置附近往复；声源停止后，已经发出的波仍会继续传播。没有适合的介质时，机械声波不能这样传播。

academic.title: 频率与振幅描述不同性质
academic.body: 频率表示每秒完成多少次振动，与简单音的音高密切相关；振幅描述偏离平衡位置的大小，与声强有关。更大的振幅通常带来更响的声音，但响度还依赖频率、距离和听觉。画面把位移和时间放大，便于观察，播放的合成音保留模型频率，不能用慢镜头里数到的摆动次数当实际音高。

academic.title: 理想弦模型的适用条件
academic.body: 固定两端的理想弦基频为 f = (1/2L)√(T/μ)，其中 L 是长度，T 是张力，μ 是线密度。只有其余条件不变，张力增至四倍才使频率变为两倍。真实橡皮筋拉伸时长度、粗细和材料性质也会改变，并具有阻尼与非线性；本页固定两端位置与线密度，单独比较张力，不求解真实拉伸橡皮筋的频谱。空气视图用同一振动在不同位置的延迟，表示因果传播，并以位移梯度表示压缩与稀疏。

zh.misconception: 更响不必更高；画里的慢摆动也不是实际听到的每秒振动次数。
zh.boundary: 慢镜头中的时间、位移与声速不是现实比例；空气小团示意忽略热运动、三维扩散和反射。音频是单独点击播放的合成音，暂停画面不会暂停现实声波。改变实验条件会从头开始。

narration.label: 听声音，也看振动
narration.text: 橡皮筋来回动，会推动旁边的空气。先播放慢镜头，再切换到空气，看看变化怎样一段一段传向远处。金色小团的家在空心圈那里，它只在家附近来回，没有一路跑到耳朵。画面特意放慢了；如果想听真实的音高，再点一下听声音的按钮。
narration.cue: 播放慢镜头，切到空气，在金色点离开空心圈时暂停；单独点击音频。

narration.label: 先只改变绷紧程度
narration.text: 现在我们只把绷紧程度调高一点，再拨一下。听起来是不是更高了一些？先停一下，换回刚才的条件再听一次，比较会更容易。在这个简化实验中，绷紧程度改变了来回振动的快慢。真实橡皮筋还有长短、粗细这些条件，会一起影响声音。
narration.cue: 比较两种张力，播放之间留三秒。

narration.label: 再改变拨动幅度
narration.text: 这回把绷紧程度保持不变，只让拨动幅度大一点。你听到的主要是更响，还是更高呢？幅度是在说动得有多大，频率是在说一秒来回多少次，它们是两件不同的事。我们可以慢慢比较，不需要把声音开很大，也不要把耳朵贴近扬声器。
narration.cue: 固定张力，比较两种幅度。

narration.label: 声源停了，路上的变化呢
narration.text: 把进度拖到后半段。橡皮筋已经不动了，可是路上还有一小段变化继续往前走。它也需要时间呀！再往后看，空气小团又回到原来的位置。我们按暂停，是让这幅慢镜头停下来，真实的声波可不会等我们。你还可以来回拖着看，找到空气挤紧和散开的位置。
narration.cue: 在空气视图回看第 9—14 秒；暂停检查源已静止而右侧仍有疏密变化。

en.question: Does tightening a band change the sound in the same way as plucking it farther?
en.observe: Play slow motion and switch to air. Follow the gold parcel relative to its open circle. Pause and review the interval after the source stops; separately compare actual audio at different tensions or amplitudes.

academic.title: Sound carries disturbances through a medium
academic.body: A vibrating band creates pressure and density disturbances in nearby air. Airborne sound is longitudinal: mean parcel displacement is parallel to propagation, unlike transverse string motion. Dots represent average parcel positions, not individual molecular thermal trajectories. Energy propagates while parcels oscillate locally. A previously emitted wave keeps traveling after its source stops; such mechanical waves need a suitable medium.

academic.title: Frequency and amplitude differ
academic.body: Frequency counts cycles per second and relates closely to the pitch of a simple tone. Amplitude measures displacement and relates to intensity. Perceived loudness also depends on frequency, distance and hearing. Motion is enlarged and slowed while the synthesized audio retains the model frequency, so visual cycle counts are not the audible frequency.

academic.title: Conditions of the ideal-string model
academic.body: For an ideal fixed-end string, f = (1/2L)√(T/μ), with length L, tension T and linear density μ. Quadrupling tension doubles frequency only with other quantities fixed. Real rubber changes length, thickness and material behavior as it stretches. The diagram fixes endpoints and linear density to isolate tension. Delayed source motion represents causal air propagation, with the displacement gradient determining compression and rarefaction.

en.misconception: Louder need not mean higher pitched, and slow visual motion is not the actual audible frequency.
en.boundary: Visual time, displacement and propagation speed are not to physical scale. Air parcels omit thermal motion, 3D spreading and reflections. Separate audio is synthesized; pausing the diagram does not freeze real sound waves. Changing conditions restarts the experiment.

narration.label: Hear and watch
narration.text: The band moves back and forth and pushes nearby air. Start slow motion, then switch to air and follow the disturbance outward. The open circle marks the gold parcel’s home. It moves near home instead of running all the way to your ear. Our picture is deliberately slow. Click the audio button separately to hear the actual pitch.
narration.cue: Play, switch to air and pause when the gold parcel leaves its home circle; click audio separately.

narration.label: Change tension first
narration.text: Increase only the tension and pluck again. Does the note sound higher? Pause and compare it with the previous setting. In this simplified experiment tension changes how quickly the band vibrates. A real rubber band also changes length and thickness, which can influence its sound together.
narration.cue: Compare two tension settings with three seconds between plays.

narration.label: Then change amplitude
narration.text: Keep tension fixed and increase only the plucking amplitude. Is the main change loudness or pitch? Amplitude means how far something moves, while frequency means how many cycles happen each second. They describe different things. Compare at a comfortable volume, without putting your ear next to the speaker.
narration.cue: Hold tension and compare two amplitudes.

narration.label: After the source stops
narration.text: Move to the later part of the timeline. The band has stopped, but a disturbance is still traveling. That takes time too! Later the air parcels return to their original positions. Pause freezes our picture; a real sound wave would not wait for us. Scrub back and forth to find compressed and spread-out regions.
narration.cue: Review seconds 9–14 in the air view; pause with a still source and a moving disturbance farther right.

references.title: OpenStax · Sound and longitudinal air motion
